paragraphs.text: Hello, elders and sisters. Hopefully you're enjoying a Sabbath day. Hopefully most of you have been able to have the ordinance of the sacrament. For those of you that haven't been able to enjoy that privilege today, please know that the Lord takes your desires to be your actions in the situation that we're in at this point in time. So don't at all worry about that. Just go forward knowing that your covenant is just as efficacious, just as powerful, because if it was within your power, you would have done it.

Alright, I'm so proud of you all. I'm so excited. It was great for me to be able to see some of you yesterday. I mentioned in the podcast yesterday that that was a delight for me and I look forward to having a little more of that experience tomorrow on Monday. But now we've got a fairly lengthy podcast to cover if we want to get through the material that I want to get through before District Conferences start, because I'll be digging into this in my workshop in District Conferences, so I want to give you the background to where we're going to be going before they start on Tuesday. So bear with me. This is going to be probably a 20 or 25-minute podcast. I appreciate your attention. I know these are not as easy to listen to. There's more deep stuff here. It's a little more dense and not so easily comprehended or entertaining. But the key is there's power here. And as you gain understanding here, even if you have to work at it a little harder, that understanding is going to be a blessing in your life.

So let's begin where we left off, which is the gifts of the Spirit. Because what we really want to focus on is learning how we can actually enhance our ability to do the things that we want to do, to increase our ability to succeed. So as we analyze this quickly, what we see is that achieving our goals, achieving the things that we want to have in our life that are good and righteous, requires sometimes capacities beyond our natural ability. And this is the very reason why the Lord has provided for what he calls in the scriptures gifts of the Spirit.

Generally, your ability to achieve goals, or we might say your righteous desires, will be greatly enhanced if you first seek the gifts of the Spirit. The gifts of the Spirit are at your disposal to help you develop your full potential. The Lord expects you to earnestly seek gifts of the Spirit through faith. In D&C 46:8, we read: "Seek ye earnestly the best gifts..." In D&C 11 verse 10: "Behold, thou hast a gift, or thou shalt have a gift if thou wilt desire of me in faith, with an honest heart, believing in the power of Jesus Christ, or in my power which speaketh unto thee." And this one from Moroni chapter 10, verses 18 and 19: "And I would exhort you, my beloved brethren, that ye remember that every good gift cometh of Christ. And I would exhort you, my beloved brethren, that ye remember that he is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that all these gifts of which I have spoken, which are spiritual, never will be done away, even as long as the world shall stand, only according to the unbelief of the children of men."

Throughout your life, consistently remind yourself that the gifts of the Spirit are given of God unto men and women to profit them. The gifts of the Spirit are at your disposal to assist you in all aspects of your life if you seek them. It's not just for religious matters or spiritual things. For example, there will be times in your life when you'll be required to put in long hours in connection to your employment or your church assignments or your family. You are entitled to a gift of the Spirit which will result in a literal renewal of your body. The Lord has promised that if you exercise faith and request it, you, quote, "shall not be weary in mind, neither in body, limb, nor joint," close quote. That's in D&C 84 verse 80.

Even though the gift of the Holy Ghost is conferred upon people when they're confirmed members of the Church, they still have the responsibility to prayerfully seek the gift. Receipt of the gift of the Holy Ghost is not automatic. In the course of our lives, we need to seek the specific gifts associated with the gifts of the Holy Ghost. For instance, the power of recall, being able to remember, a sure witness of the divinity of Christ, being comforted, and other gifts that you know are a part of the gift of the Holy Ghost.

Members of the Church who have callings as teachers should earnestly seek those gifts of the Spirit that will make them effective as teachers. In Moroni 10:7 through 10, you get a great example of that. And also this idea right here that's illuminated for us in D&C 42: "And the Spirit shall be given unto you by the prayer of faith; and if ye receive not the Spirit ye shall not teach." That's both a commandment and a prediction. If you don't have the Spirit, you're not going to teach. And if you don't have the Spirit, you shouldn't be trying to teach. And so instead of just giving up, you should go back, exercise your repentance and faith to get the Spirit. Missionaries especially should seek the gift of the Spirit that will give them the power to convince people that the Gospel of Jesus Christ has been restored to the earth.

One gift every member of the Church of Jesus Christ should seek is the gift of discernment. Each of you as a full-time missionary should have been blessed with the gift of discernment when you were set apart as a missionary. However, this is much like being blessed in the receipt of the Holy Ghost. You still have to work at it. As a member of the Church, you are given the basic gifts of discernment through the Light of Christ and the gift of the Holy Ghost. You are endowed with the ability to discern between good and evil, whether or not a person is righteous, and when the Spirit of God is being manifest. If you are desirous and earnestly seek it, if you strive to cultivate the Spirit of discernment, you will be endowed with even greater powers of discernment.

If you are successful in cultivating this keener discernment, quote, "the thoughts and intents of the hearts of the people will be revealed to your mind. Do you not know that you need the Spirit of the Almighty to look through a man and discern what is in his heart while his face smiles upon you and his words flow as smoothly as oil?" close quote. That's from the president of the Church, Brigham Young. And I've personally witnessed the power of this in my business dealings, being able to discern between those who would be good business partners and those who would not be, even though their talents and their presentations were very exceptional.

Again, from the Journal of Discourses, teachings of Brigham Young, quote, "The revelations of the Lord Jesus Christ, the Spirit of truth, will detect everything. It will lead to God, the fountain of light, where the gate will be open and the mind will be enlightened so that we shall see, know, and understand things as they really are." Further quoting Brigham Young: "I rejoice in the privilege of meeting with the Saints and hearing them speak and enjoying the influence that is within and around them. That influence opens to my understanding the true position of those who are endeavoring to serve their God. I do not require to hear them speak to enable me to know their feelings. Is it not also your experience that when you meet persons in the street, in your houses, in your offices, or in the workshops, more or less of an influence attends them which conveys more than words can? This knowledge is obtained through that invisible influence which attends intelligent beings and betrays the atmosphere in which they delight to live."

The power of discernment is evidenced many times in the scriptures. I can give you a reference of these and will in our district conference. If in your association with other people you're able to discern their thoughts and feelings, your ability to know what to say and do will be greatly increased. Also, we are entitled to discern when people are evil or designing. Also, the gift of discernment is at your disposal to assist you in every responsibility, whether it be secular like work or school or social activities or in your religious and church assignments. However, you must request the gift and tell the Lord why you want the gift, as well as explain what you will do with the gift if he bestows it upon you. Once you receive and cultivate the gift of discernment, your spiritual capabilities will be dramatically enhanced and you will be able to function with inspiration in all areas of your life.

The nature of the gifts of the Spirit themselves appear to be virtually unlimited. Faith itself is a gift of the Spirit. The nature of the gifts of the Spirit seem to grow out of specific needs, so it would not serve any purpose to try to list them. However, the gift of the Spirit which is the greatest of all is charity. We are admonished to seek this gift with all the energy of our hearts. Moroni admonishes us to cleave—which means to adhere or to cling, to hold on to tightly—he says to cleave unto charity. He also taught us that if in the final analysis a man does not have charity, quote, "he is nothing," close quote.

A person who cultivates the gift of charity will evidence certain characteristics. He will be long-suffering. He will be kind. He will not envy. He will not be puffed up. He will serve the interests of others. He will not be easily provoked. He will not think about evil things. He will rejoice in the truth. He will bear the infirmities and afflictions of this mortal life. He will believe all the truths associated with the gospel of Jesus Christ. He will evidence a prevailing hope in all the promises made in the holy scriptures. He will endure all things without wavering in his commitment to the Lord Jesus Christ.

If any of us are imperfect, it is our duty to pray for the gift that will make us perfect. Have I imperfections? I am full of them. What is my duty? To pray to God to give me the gifts that will correct these imperfections. If I'm an angry man, it is my duty to pray for charity, which suffers long and is kind. If I'm an envious man, it is my duty to seek for charity, which envies not. And so it is with all the gifts of the gospel; they are intended for this purpose. No man ought to say, "Oh, I cannot help this; it's my nature." He's not justified in saying that for the reason that God has promised to give strength to correct these things and to give gifts that will eradicate those weaknesses.

Elder Bruce R. McConkie taught, quote, "Spiritual gifts are endless in number and infinite in variety. Those that are listed in the revealed scriptures are simply examples," close quote. Dallin H. Oaks taught that the gifts of the Spirit, quote, "can lead us to God. They can shield us from the power of the adversary. They can compensate for our inadequacies and repair our imperfections," close quote. Elder Orson F. Pratt of the Quorum of the Twelve said, quote, "Spiritual gifts are distributed among the members of the Church according to their faithfulness, circumstances, natural abilities, duties, and callings, that the whole may be properly instructed, confirmed, perfected, and saved. The gifts of the Spirit will be yours: one, if you acquire the necessary insight about and understanding of the gifts of the Spirit; two, if you desire them; three, if you ask the Lord to grant you the gifts; and four, if you comply with the laws that govern the powers of heaven."

Quote, "A man who has none of the gifts has no faith, and he deceives himself if he supposes he has." That is from the Prophet Joseph Smith in Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith. As we look at this, we begin to see very quickly that the gifts of the Spirit are available to us and the Lord longs to give them to us, but we again have to qualify through this process of exercising faith as a principle of action and a principle of power.

As we conclude this podcast, there's one more element that we want to dive into here and that is how bold and specific we need to be. Too many members of the Church are very, very general when it comes to their communications and petitions to the Lord. Once you've made a decision about what you want the Lord to help you accomplish, your next step is to plead your case before the Lord. Go to the Lord in earnest prayer. Explain your rationale in selecting your particular desire, but most important, explain in great detail why you want the particular desire to be realized. Throughout history, we see that the Lord is responsive to the requests of mortal men if they go to him in faith and can present a strong case for the blessing they are seeking. In a very literal sense, you need to learn to reason with the Lord.

A good example of this process is found in the 11th chapter of Helaman and it bears quoting now. Alright, quote: "And it came to pass that when Nephi saw that the people had repented and did humble themselves in sackcloth, he cried again unto the Lord, saying: O Lord, behold this people repenteth, and they have swept away the band of Gadianton from among them insomuch that they have become extinct, and they have concealed their secret plans in the earth. Now, O Lord, because of this their humility wilt thou turn away thine anger, and let thine anger be appeased in the destruction of those wicked men whom thou hast already destroyed? O Lord, wilt thou turn away thine anger, yea, thy fierce anger, and cause that this famine may cease in this land? O Lord, wilt thou hearken unto me, and cause that it may be done according to my words, and send forth rain upon the face of the earth, that she may bring forth her fruit, and her grain in the season of grain? O Lord, thou didst hearken unto my words when I said, Let there be a famine, that the pestilence of the sword might cease; and I know that thou wilt even at this time hearken unto my words, for thou saidst that: If this people repent I will spare them. Yea, O Lord, and thou seest that they have repented, because of the famine and the pestilence and the destruction which has come upon them. And now, O Lord, wilt thou turn away thine anger, and try again if they will serve thee? And if so, O Lord, thou canst bless them according to thy words which thou hast said," close quote. That's Helaman 11:9 through 16. That is a powerful example of a man reasoning with the Lord in faith and confidence, and of course the Lord responded.

As you study the life of Joseph Smith, you will find that he never did receive new doctrine or new understandings until he exerted himself and went to the Lord and requested understanding or clarification on a particular point. The prophet Alma said: "Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good." When you are seeking the powers of heaven to assist you in realizing a righteous desire, you should plead your case to your Heavenly Father daily until your desire is realized. In your relationship with your Father in heaven, you must ask in order to receive.

Members of the Church have a tendency to be too general in their petitions to God. "Please bless, please help." No, you should resolve to be more specific in your requests, expressing much more specifically the desires for which you are striving. Being more specific in prayers on a regular basis enhances the chance that your prayers will become earnest and sustained by faith. Unfortunately, many people do not petition the Lord unless they're faced with some kind of a crisis. You will find that your relationship with your Father in heaven will be greatly enhanced if you are consistently seeking his help regarding your selected righteous desires instead of desires that grow out of some crisis in your life.

Obviously, if you are seeking and experiencing the Lord's help on a daily basis, then when you are faced with a crisis, your ability to exercise faith sufficient to call down the powers of heaven will be that much greater. It is man's tendency, however, to forget his dependence upon God when he's not faced with hardship or some kind of crisis. In Helaman we read again: "And because of this their great wickedness, and their boastings in their own strength, they were left in their own strength; therefore they did not prosper, but were afflicted, and smitten, and driven before the Lamanites, until they had lost possession of almost all their lands." It's Helaman 4:13. In Helaman 12:1 we read another powerful description of people who forget their dependence upon the Lord: "And thus we can behold how false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men; yea, we can see that the Lord in his great infinite goodness doth bless and prosper those who put their trust in him." And then again from the Doctrine and Covenants in section 101 verses 7 and 8: "They were slow to hearken unto the voice of the Lord their God; therefore, the Lord their God is slow to hearken unto their prayers, to answer them in the day of their trouble. In the day of their peace they esteemed lightly my counsel; but, in the day of their trouble, of necessity they feel after me."

The truly elect of God are those individuals who do not forget their dependence upon God even when they are not faced with adversity. You should make every effort, elders and sisters, to make your daily prayers earnest even when you are not facing pressing problems. Your prayers will be mighty prayers if they are persuasive, because a mighty prayer is one that is heard and answered. If your prayers are not being answered, it may be due to your failure to pray with the power of faith or sufficiently plead your case before the Lord.

A critical factor in your effort to be effective when you plead your case before the Lord is your ability to recognize your own weaknesses. If you are successful in drawing close to the Lord, your perception of your weaknesses will be very clear. Quote, "If men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness..." If you have an abiding faith in the Lord's desire to bless and assist you, you will be motivated to strive to overcome your weaknesses. The Lord is responsive if he sees evidence that a person is going to be more resolved to keep the commandments, willing to be generous with his means in supporting the kingdom of God, and in all other ways being helpful to the Lord's purposes in this mortal world.

Our relationship with God is governed by laws. God is never inconsistent. He's never willy-nilly or capricious in his disposition to bless us. He will always bless us according to our faith and worthiness. If God's dealings with men were not totally consistent, he would cease to be God. In your effort to solicit the Lord's help in realizing your righteous desires, you cannot rely on vocal prayers alone. You must learn to offer frequent silent prayers. From D&C 19:28 we read: "And again, I command thee that thou shalt pray vocally as well as in thy heart..." When you encounter a situation that causes you to doubt his willingness to bless you, or you are unable to recall his numerous promises in the scriptures that if we ask in our faith he will bless us, then your prayer should be for the Lord to help you build a stronger attitude of faith.

Elders and sisters, this concludes our podcast today. Tomorrow we will deal with the final part of this book that I'm going to share with you, but I hope that you will learn these key elements in this particular podcast today because it will bless your life forever. I look forward to talking with you all tomorrow and then of course in our district conferences throughout the balance of the week. Have a good night. We love you.
